title: Local lazy val captured by a lambda inside a local def in a method with a @specialized type parameter is rejected with "found Int, required x.type"
oracle: the program with every @specialized removed compiles and prints Some(1)
generator: wave4/harness/erasure (Gen.scala, Driver.scala): block with a local lazy val of the method type parameter and a local def returning a lambda that reads it
signature: novc|run-throw/compile-error|type mismatch; (first seen through the value-class rewrite, because methods of a value class are not specialized)
detail: def m[@specialized(Int) B](p: B) declares lazy val x: B = p and def loc(q: Int): B => B = (y: B) => x. The compiler reports "type mismatch; found: Int; required: x.type" at the reference to x inside the lambda. The error comes from retyping the duplicated body for the Int variant. A lambda that reads the lazy val directly in the method body, without the enclosing local def, compiles and runs, as does the generic method. The mechanism was not traced further.
fix_sketch: Not established; the reference to the local lazy val in the duplicated tree should be typed at the widened type B (here Int) as it is outside the local def. No compatibility cost: the program does not compile today.
